question: Where have the remains of Godibada (Dockyard) been found in the Indus Valley Civilization?
solution:
**The correct answer is - __Lothal__**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__ **

__
 
• **Lothal__**

 __
 
• Lothal is a significant site of the **Indus Valley Civilization__**, located in present-day Gujarat, India.
 
• This site is renowned for its **__well-planned dockyard__**, which suggests advanced maritime trade practices during the Harappan era.
 
• The dockyard at Lothal is considered one of the **__earliest known artificial docks__** globally, showcasing the engineering prowess of the Harappans.
 
• It was strategically located near the Gulf of Khambhat, facilitating trade and commerce through sea routes.
 
 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] __Additional Information__ **

__
 
• **Other Indus Valley sites__**

 __
 
• **Kalibangan__**

 __
 
• Famous for its fire altars and ploughed field patterns, indicating agricultural practices.
 
 
 
• **Mohenjo Daro__**
 __
 
• Known for the Great Bath and advanced urban planning, including drainage systems.
 
 
 
• **Banawali__**
 __
 
• Important for its evidence of rural Harappan settlements and pottery artifacts.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Significance of dockyards__**
 __
 
• Dockyards like the one at Lothal indicate the **importance of trade__** in the Harappan economy.
 
• They highlight the use of **__water transport__** for goods and materials such as beads, shells, and semi-precious stones.
